name: nanoclaw-aio
description: NanoClaw is a Telegram-first AI agent orchestrator for running Claude-powered assistant workflows from chat. All-In-One Unraid Edition `nanoclaw-aio` packages NanoClaw v2 into one Unraid-first container and uses the paired [code]jsonbored/nanoclaw-agent[/code] helper image for isolated agent work. Quick Install (Beginners) 1. Install this template and leave [code]Appdata Directory[/code] and [code]Host Appdata Path[/code] aligned unless you intentionally use a custom appdata path. 2. Set [code]TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN[/code] from BotFather. 3. Set [code]ANTHROPIC_API_KEY[/code] or one of the advanced Claude credential options. 4. Start the container and watch the logs for [code]PAIR_TELEGRAM_CODE[/code]. 5. Send that pairing code to your Telegram bot to pair the main chat. Power Users (Advanced View) - Advanced View exposes Claude credential aliases, OneCLI gateway settings, helper image overrides, concurrency/timeouts, logging, and assistant identity controls. - Keep [code]CONTAINER_IMAGE[/code] and [code]CONTAINER_IMAGE_BASE[/code] on the JSONbored defaults unless you build and maintain your own compatible agent helper image. - [code]NANOCLAW_HOST_APPDATA_DIR[/code] must match the host-side path for [code]/appdata[/code] because nested helper containers are launched through the host Docker daemon. Important Notes - This template is marked beta while the NanoClaw v2 runtime gets more real-world Unraid soak time. - The Docker socket mount is an advanced opt-in setting because NanoClaw launches paired helper containers through the host Docker daemon, which grants host-level Docker control. NanoClaw cannot run helper containers until that mount is enabled. - Persistent databases, logs, groups, env files, and channel state live under [code]/appdata[/code].

paths.name: Appdata Directory
paths.description: Persistent NanoClaw data: databases, logs, groups, channel state, env files, and host-visible runtime files for nested agent containers.

paths.name: Docker Socket
paths.description: Advanced opt-in security-sensitive mount. NanoClaw v2 needs the Docker socket to spawn nested jsonbored/nanoclaw-agent helper containers, which grants host-level Docker control access.

variables.name: Telegram Bot Token
variables.description: Bot token from @BotFather. After startup, send the PAIR_TELEGRAM_CODE from the logs to this bot.

variables.name: Anthropic API Key
variables.description: Claude API key. Use this or one of the advanced Claude credential options.

variables.name: Host Appdata Path
variables.description: Host-side path matching the Appdata Directory mount. Nested agent containers need this host path when the AIO talks to the host Docker daemon.

variables.name: Claude Code OAuth Token
variables.description: Optional Claude Code OAuth-style credential. Use instead of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when applicable.

variables.name: Anthropic Auth Token
variables.description: Optional Claude/Anthropic auth token for runtimes that expect ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.

variables.name: Anthropic Base URL
variables.description: Optional Anthropic-compatible API endpoint override.

variables.name: OneCLI URL
variables.description: Optional OneCLI gateway URL for NanoClaw agent credential injection.

variables.name: OneCLI API Key
variables.description: Optional OneCLI API key.

variables.name: Agent Image
variables.description: Helper image used for spawned agent containers. Advanced users may point this to a custom built agent image.

variables.name: Agent Image Base
variables.description: Base repository NanoClaw uses when building per-agent customized helper images.

variables.name: Container Timeout
variables.description: Agent container timeout in milliseconds.

variables.name: Idle Timeout
variables.description: Idle timeout in milliseconds for keeping agent containers warm after results.

variables.name: Max Output Size
variables.description: Maximum captured output from an agent container in bytes.

variables.name: Max Messages Per Prompt
variables.description: Maximum message history items NanoClaw passes into a prompt.

variables.name: Max Concurrent Containers
variables.description: Maximum number of concurrent NanoClaw agent containers.

variables.name: Log Level
variables.description: NanoClaw log level.

variables.name: Assistant Name
variables.description: Assistant trigger name used by NanoClaw. Example trigger: @nanoclaw

variables.name: Assistant Has Own Number
variables.description: Set true only when your NanoClaw assistant has its own dedicated channel identity.

variables.name: Auto Pair Telegram
variables.description: When true, the container starts the pairing-code watcher on first boot.

variables.name: Timezone
variables.description: Timezone used by scheduled tasks and formatted timestamps.
